correctness.notes: oracle passed on every measured cell | phase 3 final evaluation, harness 0.10, nodes gb200-nvl4-ts2-99

low_level: Registers 23 to 225 over the 200 distinct kernels behind the card's cells (2 with register spills, a kernel measured in more than one batch counts once), shared memory 48 to 33024 bytes, harness 0.10 on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99.
Adapter statics: input arrangement blocked, output indices, temp storage 4 to 4 bytes.
Oracle battery (23 cases per cell plus the measurement seeds) passed on every cell that has a number, no cell unsupported, no cell failed the oracle.
algorithmic: Random input (the one-node matrix on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): latency not_guaranteed wins 11 of 18 cells (runner-up in 1), latency prefer_smaller_index wins 7 of 12 cells (runner-up in 1), throughput not_guaranteed wins 13 of 18 cells (6 as W2_packed_sw_v2@T4, 4 as W2_packed_sw_v2@T8, 3 as W2_packed_sw_v2@T16, runner-up in 3), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 7 of 12 cells (3 as W2_packed_sw_v2@T8, 2 as W2_packed_sw_v2@T4, 2 as W2_packed_sw_v2@T16, runner-up in 3).

Where it wins on random input (bf16 N 32, bf16 N 128, fp32 N 8, fp32 N 16, fp32 N 32, fp32 N 64, fp32 N 128), the median margin over the runner-up is +30 percent and over the scope's reference control +277 percent.

Largest random-input deficits (distinct cells, worst regime): bf16 N 128 k 64 +158 percent behind N5_rows_fs_sub@T16 in throughput prefer_smaller_index, fp32 N 128 k 64 +157 percent behind N10_auto_sub@T16 in latency prefer_smaller_index, fp32 N 8 k 4 +77 percent behind W1_eager_same_sub@T4 in latency not_guaranteed, fp32 N 32 k 16 +55 percent behind N10_auto_sub@T16 in latency not_guaranteed.
Named workloads won on random input: deepseek_v3_group_select, deepseek_v3_group_top2, moba_32k_b512_top3, moe_dbrx, moe_gpt_oss_20b, moe_mixtral_8x7b.
negative: The GB200 pass measured random input only on one host (gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): the tie_heavy, shuffled-tie and phase 3b order-check findings for this adapter are on its B200 card.
surprises: Every lane count of the named sub-warp cells was measured on the one GB200 host, the single-host evidence for the lane-count choice that B200 lacks (its 8 and 16 lane named rows are a cross-node addendum).
open_questions: B200 pass (WINNERS_b200.md, random input on umbriel-b200-047, tie_heavy on 068, shuffled ties on 094, phase 3b on 047): the warp and sub-warp winners agree with GB200 on 359 of 376 common cells (365 of 376 when each cell is compared through the adapters both passes measured, as section 16 of the knowledge base does), the differences are named sub-warp lane-count cells, N 128 sub-warp throughput cells and warp ties within 5 percent, and in the block matrices the B1_idx against B1_det2 throughput ties fall either way. On GB200 the k 64 cells at 128 threads run 3 to 15 percent slower than on B200 (hw-researcher, a generation property) and the aarch64 cicc emits branches for the conditional swaps (T20, 3 to 4 percent).
